10.1088/1361-648x/aeb217.abstract: Abstract Since its experimental discovery as an intrinsic antiferromagnetic topological insulator in 2019, the MnBi 2 Te 4 family of materials has greatly propelled the development of condensed matter physics over the past several years. This family naturally integrates long-range magnetic order with topological band structure within a two-dimensional van der Waals layered material, providing an unprecedentedly clean platform for exploring quantum phenomena such as axion insulators, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, and the topological magnetoelectric effect. However, the transition from fundamental research to practical applications, particularly the realization of high-temperature quantum effects, is confronted with severe challenges in intrinsic defects, magnetic ground-state tuning, and electronic structure engineering. This article aims to review the current development status of the MnBi 2 Te 4 family, focusing on its core quantum phenomena, recent revolutionary breakthroughs in sample preparation techniques, and diverse tuning methods. On this basis, we outline possible pathways toward high-temperature quantum effects through innovations in material synthesis, interface engineering, and multi-strategy tuning and heterostructure engineering.
10.1088/1361-648x/aeb217.title: The challenging path toward high-temperature quantum anomalous hall effect in MnBi 2 Te 4

10.1016/j.jmmm.2026.174616.abstract: The anomalous Hall conductivity of the bulk ferrimagnetic Heusler alloy Mn 2 PtSn is calculated using density functional theory combined with maximally localized Wannier functions. The corresponding Berry curvature distributions are then computed, from which the net anomalous Hall conductivity is obtained. To enhance the anomalous Hall conductivity through symmetry reduction, three energetically stable (001) surface terminations of Mn 2 PtSn are considered, and their Berry curvature distributions are compared with those of the bulk unit cell. The increased number of Berry curvature peaks at the surface terminations leads to a higher value of the anomalous Hall conductivity. The anomalous Hall conductivity is also evaluated as a function of the Fermi level, and the presence of sharp peaks near the Fermi level indicates the potential for further enhancement through Fermi-level tuning. The high value of anomalous Hall conductivity at the surfaces highlights their potential for application in thin-film memory devices, where surface-driven properties are crucial. • Anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) of bulk and (001) Mn 2 PtSn surfaces is calculated. • Surface-induced symmetry-breaking enhances the AHC. • The Pt full monolayer shows the enhanced Berry curvature and AHC due to strong spin–orbit interaction. • AHC peak near Fermi level suggests potential for further AHC enhancement via tuning.
10.1016/j.jmmm.2026.174616.title: Surface-enhanced anomalous Hall conductivity in ferrimagnetic Mn2PtSn Heusler alloy

10.1038/s41467-026-78519-4.abstract: Abstract Strong-field terahertz (THz) excitations enable dynamic control over electronic, lattice and symmetry degrees of freedom in quantum materials. Here, we uncover pronounced terahertz-induced symmetry modulations and coherent phonon dynamics in the van der Waals antiferromagnet MnPS 3 , in which inversion symmetry is broken by its antiferromagnetic spin configuration. Our time-resolved second harmonic generation measurements reveal long-lived giant oscillations in the antiferromagnetic phase, with amplitudes comparable to the equilibrium signal, driven by phonons involving percent-level atomic displacements relative to the equilibrium bond lengths. The temporal evolution of the rotational anisotropy patterns indicates a dynamic breaking of mirror symmetry, modulated by two vibrational modes at 1.7 THz and 4.5 THz, with the former corresponding to a hidden mode not observed in equilibrium spectroscopy. These effects arise in part from a field-induced charge rearrangement mechanism that lowers the local crystal symmetry and couples to the phonon modes. We uncover a long-lived field-driven response with a complex THz polarization dependence, consistent with a metastable state of reduced symmetry. Through comparison with simulations, we interpret this response in terms of a potential antiferromagnetic-to-ferrimagnetic transition. Our results establish an effective field-tunable pathway for driving excitations otherwise weak in equilibrium.
10.1038/s41467-026-78519-4.title: Terahertz field-induced giant symmetry modulations in a van der Waals antiferromagnet
